facts.fact: An op-ed says the ANRPTS's Houwiyeti platform issues electronically signed digital civil-status documents (birth, marriage, divorce, death) that can be verified by QR code and the agency's digital signature.
An op-ed says the ANRPTS, created by decree 150/2010, handles registration in the population register, civil status, ID cards and passports, so one body holds both the civil and ID functions.

MRT.note: Only e-signed civil-status certificates are described; no digital registration of births or deaths is stated.
Nothing on civil servant digital skills.
Data protection appears only as a proposal; no law or authority is stated.
Digital skills mentioned only as an exclusion risk; no programme or measure.

facts.fact: An op-ed says citizens can request documents and services remotely through Houwiyeti and track requests, and that the criminal record, digitised in March 2025, can be obtained remotely via Houwiyeti and the Khadamati platform.

MRT.note: No enrolment count or share stated.
No number at birth is described.
Who operates or maintains the system is not stated.
Linking government databases to the ID is only a proposal.

facts.fact: An op-ed says the integrated system inaugurated in 2021, costing EUR 12,157,616, includes a national biometric register merging biographic and biometric data and a secure-document production system.
facts.system: Integrated population register and secure documents system

facts.fact: An op-ed says the system strengthened identity verification with fingerprints and facial recognition.
facts.system: Integrated population register and secure documents system

MRT.note: No other system is stated to check people against the ID.

facts.fact: An op-ed says the 2021 integrated system includes a national biometric register, and the ANRPTS handles registration in the population register.

MRT.note: Refugees are named only as users of expanded services; no registration or count stated.
No local civil registration office entering events digitally is described.
